findings.title: Zero-intervention self-completion with honest zero-removal outcome and triple-verified ledger

recommendations.title: Detection-only pre-flight phase with early exit on zero verified removals
recommendations.target: dead-code-sweep def: new phase between requirements and development
recommendations.description: Run knip/ts-prune/depcheck + grep verification as a cheap first phase. If verified-removals = 0, publish the ledger to S3/PR, terminate with a distinct outcome (nothing-to-remove) and skip code_reviewer/qa_verifier/ci_agent.
recommendations.expectedImpact: On this run: −3,914,782 ms of gate time (61.8% of wall) and the bulk of the $408.78; zero-yield sweeps become a ~40-min, low-cost no-op with an honest outcome label.

recommendations.title: Cadence gate on auto-triggered sweeps
recommendations.description: Before dispatching a dead-code sweep on a repo, check the workflows table and GitHub: skip if a sweep merged to the default branch < 14 days ago, or if a prior sweep PR is still open (ember: PR #56 open since 2026-08-24). Surface the skip as an event so it is visible.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Prevents the 29→8→0 diminishing-returns pattern from burning full-chain cost weekly; ember's third sweep in 14 days would not have run.

recommendations.title: Enforce blockedBy=[requirements ticket] on the sweeper ticket; emit real branch names
recommendations.description: Analyst blueprint must set blockedBy on the tier-3 (sweeper) ticket; orchestrator should reject a ticket-plan.json where a non-root ticket has blockedBy=[] while the requirements ticket is not done. Downstream tickets should reference the harness branch convention feature/<ticketId>-code-sweeper, not an aspirational chore/... name.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Closes a 3-of-3 ember wiring defect (TEAM-4230, TEAM-2859, 0ph7b1) and removes the per-agent 'ticket-named branch does not exist' reconciliation seen on TEAM-4231/4232/4233.

recommendations.title: Fix-before-verify: re-block QA/CI on open fix tickets
recommendations.description: When a reviewer files a fix ticket against the PR, add it to the QA ticket's blockedBy (and QA-filed fixes to CI's) before dispatch, so each gate verifies the corrected head.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Eliminates stale-head verification (QA on 1b399fb while TEAM-4241 in flight) and mid-run head moves (CI 16fc41d→73f0056); removes the 'resurfacing' fix class seen on TEAM-4242.

recommendations.title: Deletion-count-aware gate depth
recommendations.description: If the PR diff has --diff-filter=D = 0 and touches only ledger/config paths, run a ledger-accuracy review only (skip fresh-clone build + runtime smoke in QA; CI verifies the build once).
recommendations.expectedImpact: Preserves the ledger-accuracy catches (3 reviewer + 1 QA findings) at a fraction of 1,114,511 + 1,451,270 ms of gate compute.

recommendations.title: Sweeper re-derives any numeric claim inherited from requirements.md
recommendations.description: Counts copied from requirements into REMOVAL_LEDGER.md must be re-computed with git grep -c before commit; cite the command and result in the ledger row.
recommendations.expectedImpact: Would have avoided TEAM-4242 (464,398 ms + PR #59).

recommendations.title: Separate GitHub identity for the reviewer
recommendations.description: Use a distinct GitHub App/identity for agentcore_hub_code_reviewer so REQUEST_CHANGES is permitted on PRs authored by the sweeper token.
recommendations.expectedImpact: PR review state reflects the gate verdict; humans reading PR #58-style handoffs see CHANGES NEEDED, not a comment.

summaryMarkdown:
# Run analysis — wf_1788780725940_c2uqki
**Dead Code Sweep — tycenjmccann/ember — 2026-09-07** · defId `dead-code-sweep` · outcome `complete` · delivery `handoff` · trigger auto

## Verdict
A fully autonomous, honestly-reported **zero-removal** sweep: the 5-agent chain self-completed with 0 errors, 0 nudges, 0 WATCH interventions and 0 human wait — the first ember run since 0ph7b1 to do so — but it spent **105.6 min, 97.8M tokens and $408.78** (performance card status `alert`, 3.3x the $124 median) proving that a repo swept 8 days earlier (PR #57, 2026-08-31) had nothing left to remove. The system executed well; the workflow should not have run the full chain.

## Measured facts (compute_metrics.py)
- Wall clock: **6,333,247 ms (105.6 min)**, 11:32:07Z → 13:17:40Z. Agent work 7,688,796 ms (> wall: fix tickets ran in parallel with gates).
- Serial chain: TEAM-4229 analyst 598,536 ms (10.0 min) → TEAM-4230 sweeper **1,906,310 ms (31.8 min, 30.1% of wall — critical path)** → TEAM-4231 reviewer 1,114,511 ms (18.6 min) → TEAM-4232 QA 1,451,270 ms (24.2 min) → TEAM-4233 CI 1,349,001 ms (22.5 min).
- Fix tickets: 2 (TEAM-4241 codex_fix 849,695 ms; TEAM-4242 qa_fix 464,398 ms, tag `resurfacing` on the same path `REMOVAL_LEDGER.md`). changeRequests=0, humanReviews=[], nudges=0, errors=0, managerInterventions=[].
- Counts: 8 tickets, 53 events, 53 artifacts, 7 completions. Ticket provider Jira.
- Performance card (workflow.performance event): totalCostUsd 408.78 (median 124.02, z 2.47), personaUsd 349.41, codingUsd 59.37 (median 0, z 29.7), tokens 97,794,383 (median 16.4M, z 6.67), agentWorkMs z 4.98, loops 2.

## Deliverable
- Detection: knip 5.88.1 + ts-prune 0.10.3 + depcheck 1.4.7 run per-workspace (root + mcp/port-session). 93 candidates, every one grep-verified repo-wide (verification-grep.txt 105 KB, independently re-run on a fresh clone at f754cd3 — identical).
- Verdicts: REMOVED 0 · KEPT-USED-IN-MODULE 53 · KEPT-FRAMEWORK 26 · false-positive 12 · uncertain 1 · contract 1.
- PR #58 (feature/TEAM-4230-code-sweeper @ 1b399fb): +228/−0 REMOVAL_LEDGER.md, +21/−0 knip.jsonc, `--diff-filter=D` = 0. Landed on integration branch as 16fc41d (TEAM-4241), then PR #59 → 73f0056 (TEAM-4242). Unified handoff **PR #60** opened to main from feature/TEAM-4228-…; main untouched at f754cd3.
- Gates: reviewer CHANGES NEEDED (3 ledger-accuracy findings, 0 false-positive deletions) → QA FAIL (1 ledger-count finding; all proof commands exit 0, runtime smoke non-5xx) → CI PASS at 73f0056 (tsc root, next build, mcp:build, mcp tsc — all exit 0; re-ran full suite when head moved mid-run).
- Lasting value: `knip.jsonc` is now committed, so future ember sweeps can run knip without re-deriving config.

## Planning (68)
- Roster correct for a handoff sweep (4 agents + CI, no Ship/CD — CD_REGISTERED false). Requirements defined "full test suite" concretely for a repo with no test runner (tsc root, next build, mcp:build, mcp tsc, runtime smoke) and declared the empty-removal outcome explicitly valid (R7). Good.
- **Wiring defect, 3rd ember recurrence:** TEAM-4230 (sweeper) `blockedBy=[]`. The sweeper was invoked at 11:40:37.834Z, **92.3 s before** the analyst's agent.complete (11:42:10.105Z, `unblocked=[]`). Only the analyst's ordering discipline (requirements.md saved before the sweeper ticket was created) prevented a race on the requirements doc. Same pattern as 0ph7b1 and iczquj (TEAM-2859 blockedBy=[]). The analyst's fleet-lifetime `dependency_chain_compliance_online` = 0.18 is background consistent with this — not per-run evidence.
- **Branch-name mismatch:** all four downstream tickets named branch `chore/dead-code-sweep-2026-09-07`; the sweeper actually used `feature/TEAM-4230-code-sweeper`. Reviewer, QA and CI each had to detect and reconcile this ("Ticket-named branch … does not exist") — friction on three sessions.
- **Error seeded upstream:** requirements.md stated `dynamic ×27`; the true counts are `dynamic ×21` + `maxDuration ×6`. The sweeper copied the figure into REMOVAL_LEDGER.md:205 without verifying; QA caught it → TEAM-4242. Root cause is requirements accuracy + inherited-number trust, not sweeper detection.
- **No pre-flight "is there anything to sweep?" check.** The sweeper itself wrote at start: "PR #57 (merged 2026-08-31) already swept this repo a week ago, so I expect a thin candidate list." The workflow def has no cheap detection-only short-circuit; the full 4-gate chain ran on a diff with 0 deletions.

## Execution (70)
- Zero orchestration failures: every `orchestrator.unblocked` fired on time (TEAM-4231 @12:12:24, TEAM-4232 @12:30:58, TEAM-4233 @12:55:09), no dead sessions, no retries. This handoff shape (no release_manager) does not exhibit the missed-unblock cascade that hit all four extended-shape runs.
- Sweeper 31.8 min is legitimate work (93 candidates verified one-by-one, artifacts archived) but for zero yield. Reviewer 18.6 + QA 24.2 + CI 22.5 = **65.3 min (61.8% of wall) of gate time on a 0-deletion, ledger-only diff**.
- **Fix tickets ran concurrently with the gates they should have preceded:** TEAM-4241 (`blockedBy=[]`, 12:30:16–12:44:26) overlapped QA (12:30:58–12:55:09), so QA verified the stale head 1b399fb and had to note "TEAM-4241 in_progress, had not pushed". TEAM-4242 (12:53:27–13:01:12) overlapped CI (12:55:09–13:17:38); CI saw the head move 16fc41d→73f0056 mid-run and correctly re-ran the full suite at the final SHA. Outcome is sound only because CI was diligent — the def does not enforce fix-before-verify.
- Cost: $408.78 / 97.8M tokens for +249/−0 of markdown+config. `codingUsd` 59.37 vs median 0 indicates the codex delegation path was used heavily (sweeper ran codex for detection, and resumed the session for both fixes).

## Human-in-the-loop (reviewEfficiency 75)
- No human gates by design (handoff delivery; PR #60 left for the owning team). humanWaitTotalMs = 0.
- Agent gates did real independent verification: reviewer used a fresh clone + its own engine, confirmed REMOVED-set ∅ == deletions ∅ and the protected surface intact; QA ran the full proof suite + runtime smoke (`next start` and standalone server) on Node 20/22. Both caught genuine ledger inaccuracies (misattributed `Cli` citation at :116, wrong protocol peer for `encodeClose` at :198, `×27` mislabel at :205).
- But ROI was low: ~65 min of gate compute to correct three lines of prose in a ledger that documents *non*-removals. A deletion-count-aware gate policy (light review when `--diff-filter=D` = 0) would have preserved the accuracy check at a fraction of the cost.
- Tooling gap: reviewer could not post REQUEST_CHANGES because the GitHub token is the PR author; verdict was posted as a COMMENT review. The PR's review state therefore does not reflect the gate verdict.

## Rework (reworkDiscipline 80)
- 2 fix tickets, both ledger-text-only, both resolved first pass, both with proof commands re-run (exit 0). TEAM-4242 correctly `blockedBy` TEAM-4241 so the two edits to the same file landed serially. Sweeper honoured HANDOFF mode throughout (never merged to main, never called Pipeline tools).
- TEAM-4242 tagged `resurfacing` (same path as TEAM-4241): QA found a defect on the same file the reviewer had just fixed — because the reviewer's three findings did not include the count error and QA reviewed the pre-fix head. Not a fix-induced regression, but a sign the two gates overlapped rather than layered.
- Root causes: F1/F2 = sweeper citation accuracy; F3 = process ambiguity about who lands the PR on the integration branch ("If the harness performs that merge automatically … say so and skip"); TEAM-4242 = inherited requirements error. None were detection false positives — the core sweep was correct.

## Trend
- Ember has now been swept 3x in 14 days: 0ph7b1 (2026-08-24, 29 items, PR #56 still open/unmerged), iczquj (2026-08-31, 8 items, PR #57 merged), c2uqki (2026-09-07, **0 items**). Diminishing returns are complete; weekly auto-cadence on this repo is now pure cost. Note PR #56 remains open — its 29 removals never landed, so a later sweep may re-discover them once #56 is closed or rebased.
- vs iczquj (most recent ember, overall 85): wall −34,085,697 ms (iczquj's 40.4M ms was human-gate + crash park), human wait −58,921,615 ms, changeRequests −2 (iczquj's were phantom double-emits), score −9. This run is *more autonomous* but *less valuable* — the score penalises a full-chain run on a zero-yield target, not agent execution.
- The `blockedBy=[]` on the sweeper ticket is now a 3-of-3 pattern on ember (0ph7b1, iczquj TEAM-2859, c2uqki TEAM-4230). Workflow-def-level, not repo-level.
- Priors in dossier: o71s0v 85, 6o493q 84, iczquj 85, dom4hd 84, 4vraf4 91 (smoke). This run: 74.

## Recommendations
1. **P0 workflow-def — detection-only pre-flight with early exit.** Add a cheap phase after requirements: run knip/ts-prune/depcheck + grep verification; if verified-removals = 0, publish the ledger, terminate with a distinct `outcome=nothing-to-remove`, and skip reviewer/QA/CI. Would have saved ~65 min and most of the $409 here.
2. **P0 process — sweep cadence gate on auto-trigger.** Do not auto-start a sweep on a repo whose last sweep (a) merged < 14 days ago or (b) still has an open sweep PR (ember: PR #56 open since 08-24, #57 merged 08-31). Check the workflows table / GitHub before dispatch.
3. **P1 workflow-def / prompt — enforce `blockedBy=[requirements]` on the sweeper ticket.** 3-of-3 ember runs shipped it empty. Either the orchestrator validates the chain on ticket-plan.json (reject a tier-3 ticket with no blocker) or the analyst blueprint is made explicit. Also make the analyst emit the *actual* branch naming convention (`feature/<ticket>-code-sweeper`) into downstream tickets instead of an aspirational `chore/…` name.
4. **P1 gate-config — fix-before-verify ordering.** When a reviewer files a fix ticket, the QA ticket should be re-blocked on it (and CI on any QA fix) so gates verify the corrected head rather than a stale one. QA verified 1b399fb while TEAM-4241 was in flight; CI absorbed a mid-run head move.
5. **P1 gate-config — deletion-count-aware review depth.** When `--diff-filter=D` = 0 and the diff touches only ledger/config, run a ledger-accuracy review only (no fresh-clone build/runtime smoke in QA, CI still verifies the build once).
6. **P2 prompt — sweeper must verify inherited counts.** Any numeric claim copied from requirements.md into the ledger must be re-derived (`git grep -c`) before commit — the `×27` mislabel originated upstream and was repeated verbatim.
7. **P2 tooling — reviewer identity.** Use a distinct GitHub identity/app for the reviewer so REQUEST_CHANGES is permitted and PR review state reflects the gate verdict.
